---
title = "Paths"
---

Paths resolve from two locations:

1. The project root, for configuration and content.
2. The document directory, for code execution.

# Project root

The project root is:

- Single document: the directory containing the `.qmd` file.
- Collection: the directory containing `index_calepin/config.toml`.

The following resolve from the project root:

- Front matter fields: `bibliography`, `csl`.
- `{% include %}` directives.
- Image paths in Markdown.
- Template overrides in `{stem}_calepin/templates/`.

In a collection, every page shares the same root, so a single path like `bibliography = "assets/library.bib"` works everywhere regardless of nesting.

# Document directory

The document directory is the parent directory of the `.qmd` file. The following resolve from there:

- Code chunk working directory (R, Python, shell).

If `posts/analysis.qmd` calls `read.csv("data.csv")`, it finds `data.csv` next to the source file.

# Build artifacts

Build artifacts are split into two directories at the project root:

- `.calepin/cache/{stem}/` -- code execution cache
- `{stem}_output/` -- rendered site (collections only)

Both directories should be in `.gitignore`. To clear them: `rm -rf .calepin/ *_output`.

# Output

- Single document: output goes alongside the input, or where `-o` specifies.
- Website: output goes to `{stem}_output/` by default (e.g., `index_output/` for a project with `index.qmd`). Configurable via the `output` field in `config.toml`.

# URL resolution {#url-resolution}

All internal URLs in site templates are page-relative. A page at `guide/intro.html` links to assets with `../assets/calepin.css`, while `index.html` uses `./assets/calepin.css`. This works on any server, any subdirectory, and from `file://`.

The `url` field in `config.toml` is only used for canonical URLs (meta tags, sitemaps, RSS feeds):

```toml
url = "https://example.com/docs/"
```

## `link()` in templates

In site templates, use the `link()` function to generate correct relative paths:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="{{ link('assets/calepin.css') }}">
<a href="{{ link('index.html') }}">Home</a>
```

`link()` computes the relative path based on the current page's nesting depth. External URLs (`https://...`), anchor links (`#...`), and data URIs pass through unchanged.

Preview (`calepin preview`) and render (`calepin render`) produce identical output.
